title: Maltravers to Ormonde, cipher passages of 13 Sept 1634 and 22 Jan 1634/5 (HMC Ormonde I, pp. 28-29)

steps.what: Letters and page scans taken from the HMC Ormonde I volume on the Internet Archive; figures checked against the scans.
Ranges separated: 91-111 nulls at run edges, 112+ standalone codes, below 91 letters; doubled letters on consecutive figures.
Regular grid of three figures per consonant from 7; exhaustive scan of 42 regular grids ranks it first.
All spelled words read; nomenclator codes glossed from context.
Nomenclator checked against Wentworth's dispatches in Knowler's Strafforde's Letters (1739): seven of nine codes fixed.

Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py): 57 tokens, 36 types, en-1640s order 4: reading -2.277 per letter; random keys -2.961 (z 3.8); key annealed onto shuffled ciphertext best -2.069 (mean -2.119, z -3.6); annealer on the real text -2.113. Verdict: underdetermined.

validation.notes: claimed per-occurrence score -2.277; polyphony 0.0; 4 unread tokens left out; annealer on the real text from random keys reached -2.113

outcome.method: key recovered based on adjacent plaintext
outcome.method_basis: The letter alphabet came from cribs in the clear English around the figures in HMC Ormonde I pp. 28-29 ('brought no letters from', 'is to be a councellor', Crosby) plus the consecutive-figure doubled letters; seven of nine nomenclator codes were then fixed from Wentworth's dispatches in Knowler 1739 (external).
outcome.notes: Two person-codes (185, 149) in one clause unidentified; vowel block boundaries not fixable.

prior.where: Tomokiyo lists as unsolved; no key or decipherment in HMC

human: Project-level: obtained a DECODE login with privileges and passed its session cookie (from the browser developer tools) to the model, set up Claude Code with Fable 5.1 or Opus 5, and posed the problem with /goal; occasionally offered encouragement or chose which of the model-identified leads to pursue. No target-specific intervention recorded.
